title: Three Killed in Armed Attack on Manipur Village as Naga-Kuki Violence Escalates
excerpt: Suspected militants opened fire on a Kuki-inhabited village in Kangpokpi, killing three and critically injuring four.
body:
• Three villagers, including two women, killed in armed attack on Kuki-inhabited N. Teikhang village in Kangpokpi district on August 31
  • Four others critically injured as suspected NSCN-IM militants opened indiscriminate fire and set houses ablaze
  • Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the attack and vowed arrests
  • More than 20 people from Naga and Kuki communities killed since inter-ethnic violence erupted in February 2026

Three villagers, including two women, were killed and four others critically injured when suspected militants attacked a Kuki-inhabited village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Monday, marking one of the deadliest single incidents in the state's ongoing ethnic violence this year.

Armed militants opened indiscriminate fire at N. Teikhang village in the mountainous district using sophisticated weapons, according to police officials in Imphal. Several houses were also set ablaze during the attack, forcing villagers, including women and children, to flee into nearby forests.

What Happened

Police initially confirmed two deaths and one injury. However, the Twilang Area Kuki CSO Working Committee said three villagers were shot dead and four others sustained bullet wounds and remained critically injured. The four injured were identified as Nemneichong Lhoujem, 50, Seilun Lhoujem, 70, Deilhing Haokip, 55, and Kamtinsei Chongloi, 38.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2094765994082521183

The Kuki tribal organisation alleged that around 50 heavily armed cadres of the separatist NSCN-IM and its alleged proxy force, ZUF-K, carried out the attack. Manipur Police and Central Armed Police Forces rushed to the area and launched operations to bring the situation under control.

"I strongly condemn the killing of three villagers, including two women and the injuries sustained by four others, including two women, at N. Teikhang village in Kangpokpi district today."

— Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Manipur Chief Minister

Escalating Naga-Kuki Violence

The attack came days after suspected militants ambushed a vehicle in the same district, killing four Naga civilians and injuring another. More than 20 people from both Naga and Kuki communities have been killed in separate firing incidents since violence broke out between the two groups in February 2026. Several houses have been burnt across the affected areas.

The Kuki Students' Organisation strongly condemned what it described as an unprovoked and barbaric assault on innocent residents. The conflict between Naga and Kuki tribal groups represents a distinct axis of violence from the Meitei-Kuki clashes that devastated the state beginning in May 2023.

Government Response

Chief Minister Singh, who was in Delhi at the time, posted his condemnation on X on Monday night. "The Government will not tolerate such violence. The culprits responsible for the killing will be arrested and punished as per the law of the land," he wrote. Security forces said additional details were being ascertained and operations were continuing in the affected area.

What Comes Next

The attack underscores the fragile security situation in Manipur's hill districts, where multiple ethnic fault lines continue to produce periodic violence despite central and state security deployments. For the Indian diaspora, the continued instability in Manipur remains a source of concern, particularly for families with roots in the northeastern state.
